Reflection summary: This question was answered correctly, and it did expose a genuinely new, generalizable pattern worth saving — the MSR (Mid-Session Review) projected-vs-actual budget deficit family.

Key generalizable insight captured:
- Unlike the regression abs-diff questions (where the "actual" is an external constant not in any document), this MSR pattern has BOTH operands inside Treasury Bulletins. The projection for FY N lives in the September YEAR-N issue, and the actual for FY N lives in the September YEAR-(N+1) issue. The question typically names both publications explicitly.
- Round each operand to hundredths first, then take the absolute difference. Output is a MODE A bare decimal (0.17).

I created `references/msr-projected-vs-actual-budget.md` with the trigger, the year-N / year-(N+1) bulletin-mapping rule, the compute recipe, and pitfalls, plus a one-paragraph pointer in SKILL.md's reference index. No memory edit needed — the durable cross-session facts (delimiter modes, abs-diff/external-actual distinction) are already covered, and this new pattern is more procedural than a one-line fact, so it belongs in the skill reference rather than the compact memory block.
